EXTRA CLASS · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY

Every place in town, with its lesson on the card.

The town-map class: twenty-eight places walk the whole town in tour order — the places that teach us, the places that keep us safe, the food-and-shopping run, the quiet squares, the ways the town moves and the green places — and every tile below opens its own simple lesson a kid can follow.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Every place in town — with a lesson on its card.

The Places in the Community class is a bonus class, kept beside the main learning path like the Kitchen Helper and the Doctor Visit: the regular classes stay the core sequence, and this one is for the days when somebody asks what is that building? Twenty-eight places a town is made of — the library, the fire station, the bakery, the bus stop, the park — each one on its own card, and each card opens a simple lesson a kid can follow: what the place is, who works there, what we do there, step by step, and one way to play it at home tonight.

The places run in tour order on purpose. The learning places come first, because school is the building your child already owns; then the helping places, where doctors, dentists and the two stations keep everyone safe; then the food-and-shopping run; the quiet squares that make a town work; the ways the town moves; and the last group is the fresh air — gardens, parks, playgrounds, the zoo. By the end, the whole map of the town sits in one deck of cards.

Twenty-eight places in six groups, in the order a real trip across town unfolds. Tap any picture and it opens its own simple lesson — the original card on the left, and the kid-followable guide on the right.

THE CLASS GAME

The Town Walk: build a street on the floor.

Stack the cards face down. Draw the top one, place it at the end of a growing "street" across the floor, and say what happens there — at the bakery, I buy bread! At the fire station, the truck sleeps! Card by card the street grows around the room until all twenty-eight places stand in a row, and then comes the best part: walk the whole town, end to end, and greet every stop on the way. Grown-ups walk it too — the losing shoe and the wrong turn are all part of the map.

SAME PLACE, TWO NAMES

Movie theater and cinema. Both are right.

Places travel even less than games do — the building never moves, but its name crosses the ocean and changes clothes. This class says so out loud. The cinema is the movie theater; the pharmacy is the drugstore or the chemist’s; the gas station sells petrol across the ocean; the dentist’s office is the dentist’s surgery in the UK; the sports center plays as the leisure centre; the shopping cart is a trolley; the garbage and trash are the rubbish; the street box is a mailbox or a post box; the pet shop is a pet store; and the airplane flies as the aeroplane. Whichever your family says, your child hears both — and learns early that places, like words, come in kinds.
